stem: An Auto Scaling group hosts an application with a multi-minute startup routine, and the platform team wants scale-out events to reach a healthy state much faster without changing the AMI.

choices.text: Configure a warm pool for the Auto Scaling group
Rely on the two-minute Spot Instance interruption notice

rationale: A warm pool keeps pre-initialized instances in a Stopped, Running, or Hibernated state outside the group's active capacity, so a scale-out event can resume an already-initialized instance instead of booting one from cold, cutting the time to become healthy without touching the AMI. Instance refresh replaces instances with new ones built from an updated launch template or AMI; it addresses rolling out a new AMI, not speeding up an individual scale-out event. A mixed instances policy widens the pool of available capacity and instance types and mixes purchase options, but it does not by itself change how long an instance takes to boot and become healthy. The two-minute Spot interruption notice only warns that a Spot Instance is about to be reclaimed; it has nothing to do with how fast a newly launched instance starts.
